section.scope_note: Labeled applications only — 2027 of 2033 in-frame live-slice applications labeled, 1991 of the labeled read from the docket alone; primaries only; not docket-representative. Those counts are raw rows (the second includes the few duplicate rows the labeling frame folds into one per docket number); the bucket counts are reweighted like every section here. The frame is the live slice's non-extension application dockets, substantive asks and asks whose kind was never read alike, read from different inputs than the petition cut, so the two are never pooled. A docket-only row whose caption and entries name no subject is `unclassifiable` by rule, so that bucket tracks how thin the dockets are as much as what the applications are about. Batch 2's extract counted 2027 application(s) in the frame it cut from, of which the artifact held 2027 labeled (100.0%); read that share as a ceiling on the share of the frame as it now stands, since the frame grows with every pull. The reference block rides in every batch, so its 241 row(s) are over-represented against the 1786 drawn from the 1786 outside it by no factor — the frame was fully labeled when that batch landed, and this mix is not the frame's until every application is labeled. Of the labeled rows here, 241 are reference-block members and 1786 were drawn.

sections.scope_note: The capital flag is latched from supremecourt.gov's own `bCapitalCase` payload field, OR-ed with the `*** CAPITAL CASE ***` annotation the same channel appends to the docket number — either alone under-reports, and no other channel serves either reading. So `last_live_polled` is the column's coverage sentinel: a row no live poll stamped buckets as `(unknown)` rather than as unmarked, and none appear here because this section is already scoped to the live slice, which is that stamp. Inside the slice the stamp records an attempted poll rather than an ingested payload, so `unmarked` means no channel that wrote the row read either signal — silence, not a denial. Read it as an upper bound: contamination runs one way, into `unmarked`, so it can only shrink the gap between these buckets, never widen it. The split is a marginal one — it describes what the two populations are, not what the marking adds over the cuts beside it.
